# Josie Pye

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Josie was considered too fat to play the role of a slender fairy queen.

_Sources: [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014)_

## Personality

Josie is disagreeable, sharp-tongued, and sulky when she does not get her way. She displays a malicious and envious disposition, frequently making spiteful remarks about others and accusing those who achieve success of cheating. Additionally, she is superstitious and known to peep at her book while at school.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c32 P7](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0007), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c37 P33](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0033), [v3 c11 P41](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0041), [v3 c16 P2](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0002)_

## History

Josie attended Avonlea school under Mr. Phillips and Miss Stacy, where she was the last of the Pye family to attend. During a school spelling match, she cheated by looking at her book, drawing Anne Shirley's scorn. She excelled at walking board fences and successfully walked the Barry fence on a dare, which she had issued after daring Jane Andrews to hop on one leg. When preparing for a local concert, Josie grew sulky because she was denied the role of fairy queen due to her figure, and she insulted Anne's hair in retaliation. Later, she ceased speaking to Julia Bell for three months after making a rude comment about Julia's recitation bow. At the Exhibition, Josie won first prize for her knitted lace. She prepared for the Queen's College entrance examinations—telling classmates she wished to attend college purely for education's sake—and went on to achieve preeminence at Queen's Academy as the sharpest-tongued student. When Anne returned to college after winning a prize story contest, Josie out of envy accused Anne of copying the story from an old paper.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 c23 P5](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0005), [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c26 P2](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0002), [v1 c29 P24](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0024), [v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c38 P40](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0040), [v3 c16 P2](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0002)_
